causes.text: In August 2023 Disney announced that it would raise the price of ad-free Disney+ by $3 to almost $14 and hike Hulu's no-ads plan by 20%, while introducing a lower-priced ad-supported tier, signalling a push for profitability amid slowing growth.

source_info.title: Disney raises US streaming prices and plans £3 monthly rise in UK

effects.text: Following competitors' price hikes, Netflix's sign-ups remained elevated and its shares gained about 1.7% as investors viewed its subscriber momentum as a competitive advantage.

source_info.title: Netflix sign-ups remain high, fueled by password-sharing crackdown

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Disney announced sizeable price increases for its ad-free Disney+ and Hulu plans, raising U.S. subscription fees by $3 and 20% respectively and encouraging customers to migrate to cheaper ad-supported tiers. The company framed the hikes as necessary to drive profitability.

Higher prices and the prospect of more adverts made the Disney streaming bundle less attractive to some subscribers. Price-sensitive viewers began re-evaluating their subscriptions and looking for better value elsewhere.

Many of these viewers opted to switch to or supplement their streaming with Netflix, which was also converting freeloaders through its password-sharing enforcement. The combination of returning users and defecting Disney customers helped keep Netflix sign-ups elevated even after the initial crackdown.

Investors interpreted the sustained sign-up momentum as evidence of Netflix's competitive strength and pricing power. As a result, the company's shares rose about 1.7% in early trading, reflecting confidence that it would capture market share from rivals.

rationale: By raising prices significantly, Disney unintentionally nudged some consumers toward Netflix, helping to maintain high sign-up levels and modestly boosting Netflix's share price.
counterfactual_analysis: Had Disney not raised prices, fewer subscribers would have defected, and Netflix's sign-ups and share price might have risen less.

adversarial_confounders.text: Netflix released a hit original series around the same time.
adversarial_confounders.impact: A popular show could independently attract new subscribers, inflating sign-up numbers irrespective of Disney's pricing decisions.

details.commentary: Disney's decision to raise streaming prices and add more ads increased the perceived cost of staying in rival ecosystems. That move nudged price sensitive viewers toward Netflix, improving its relative value proposition and helping it capture share in a crowded streaming market.

Households facing higher living costs are re-evaluating which subscriptions to keep and which to cancel. In this economic climate, aggressive price and ad load increases at competitors made Netflix's pricing and content mix more attractive without it needing to move first.

As Disney raised prices, some subscribers canceled or downgraded and looked for alternatives, feeding incremental sign ups at Netflix. That steady inflow of value seeking customers supported ongoing growth and reinforced investor confidence that Netflix could benefit from rivals' missteps.
